verdicts.note: Personality traits and timing of motherhood.
Clinical primer on infertility.
Tempo adjustment in the age-parity model. A.11's.
Quality of life in involuntarily childless couples.
Attitudes to ART across 42 European countries. Politics of access, not its effect.
No abstract. CLINIC COMPETITION and ART outcomes — market structure as a supply-side exposure. P2's cell is thin, and this is one of the few non-price supply margins in the frame.
No abstract. The ACA's effect on fertility care — a national coverage change layered on the state mandates.
No abstract. Men attending fertility counselling.

**THE IMPACT OF INFERTILITY ON FAMILY SIZE, US NSFG.** Tests whether biological fertility potential actually binds family size. A.17 assumes it does; this measures it on nationally representative data.
No abstract. ART twins' contribution to the very-preterm rate. A.12 by exposure, Wall 2 by outcome.
Single women and elective egg freezing as a response to LACK OF A PARTNER. Second record naming the partnership channel — the constraint is A.24/C.7's and the technology is A.17's.

**GERMANY: legislative change in ART reimbursement.** Germany's 2004 cut in statutory coverage is one of the sharpest downward access shocks available anywhere, and downward shocks are rare — most of arm 2 is expansions. Priority for the identification set.
No abstract. How labelling infertility affects public support for coverage.
Employer subsidisation of reproductive healthcare, normative.
Parenthood expectations among emerging adults.
Indonesian adolescents' desired family size.
Undergraduate awareness of reproductive ageing.
No abstract. Spain's TRANSNATIONAL fertility industry — cross-border access, which is PI call 3's problem in its supply-side form.
Lay views on fertility assessment methods.
COVID commentary.
Iranian preconception-care intervention.
Parenthood and the gender pay gap. The literature the AER/JPopEcon IVF-instrument papers were written for.
Review of oocyte cryopreservation's state of the art.
Phytoestrogens and male infertility. B.2's.
Portugal: fertility knowledge and INFORMATION SOURCES — the supply side again.

**RATIONING BY ELIGIBILITY: exclusion from publicly funded IVF on obesity grounds.** Non-price access restriction, which is P2's exposure and a common one — most public systems ration by BMI, age and smoking rather than by price.
Validation of self-reported assisted conception against registers. Measurement quality for the exposure series — worth citing when the chapter states how ART births are ascertained.
Evolutionary genetics of partner incompatibility.
Oncofertility capacity building in developing countries.
Content analysis of newspaper coverage of ART. Third record on the belief channel's supply side, alongside the celebrity-magazine study.
Population Studies: PROJECTED future utilisation of ART, IUI and ovulation induction in Australia. Projects the exposure rather than the births, and separates the three modalities.
Ideal versus actual intervals to first birth, Singapore.
MAR availability for people living with HIV across Europe — another non-price ELIGIBILITY restriction, and a cross-country policy comparison of exactly the kind P2 needs.
Latvian survey of satisfaction and family size.
Polish policy review of abortion and IVF.
ICSI use trends and reproductive outcomes, JAMA. Treatment-mix change with a per-cycle outcome.

**WHEN AND WHY SUBFERTILE COUPLES DISCONTINUE CARE.** Dropout is the leak between treatment access and births: a mandate that raises cycles produces no births if couples stop before success. Pairs with the mandate-and-discontinuation record in batch 5.
CDC ART Surveillance 2009.

**'PERPETUAL POSTPONERS?' — fertility INTENTIONS followed through to SUBSEQUENT FERTILITY BEHAVIOUR on BHPS panel data.** The belief-to-behaviour link P6 needs, measured longitudinally. Together with the 8-year FAC follow-up and the Austrian intentions studies, P6 now has three or four genuine behaviour-side candidates rather than none.
Wood's Dynamics of Human Reproduction. Foundational for the proximate-determinants framework, not an A.17 record.
No abstract. Long-term trends in late and very late fertility — the age band ART operates in.

A FIGURE, indexed as a work: 'Growth in numbers of ART cycles, deliveries, and infants, US 1996-2005.' Its CONTENT is exactly arm 1's exposure series, but the record is a figure caption. Another paratext artifact — the third in this screen.

**SR and meta-analysis: ~30% OF ART PATIENTS DO NOT ACHIEVE PARENTHOOD.** The conversion rate from treatment to birth, meta-analysed. Arm 1 counts the successes; this quantifies the denominator they came from.
Public-health framing of infertility.

**A DECADE OF PLANNED OOCYTE CRYOPRESERVATION: clinical outcomes AND UTILISATION.** The single most useful P5 record so far — it reports how many women returned to use frozen eggs and what came of it, which is the question the attitude studies cannot answer.
Young Australian men's views on timing.
CDC ART Surveillance 2012.
Intergenerational fertility correlation. A.19's.
FReDA panel study design paper.
Provider and patient views on paying for ART.

**'SEVEN OUT OF 10 COUPLES TREATED BY IVF ACHIEVE PARENTHOOD FOLLOWING EITHER TREATMENT, NATURAL CONCEPTION OR ADOPTION', 8-year follow-up.** This is arm 1's counterfactual stated as a finding: a large share of parenthood among treated couples arrives by routes other than the treatment. Together with the Japanese dropout study, it is the empirical core of the upper-bound argument. Highest priority in the frame.

**QUEBEC's public funding of IVF, in NEJM.** A sharp provincial policy introducing (and later withdrawing) full funding — one of the cleanest natural experiments in the access literature, and non-US. Priority.
Qualitative study of unsuccessful ART in Iran.
Childless men's family-formation intentions.
Commentary on ART program reporting — describes how NASS and SART data are collected, which is provenance for the exposure series.
Iran: fertility KNOWLEDGE against CHILDREN EVER BORN. Belief against a realized outcome, which most of this cell lacks — but cross-sectional and non-OECD.
French national registry of preservation in cancer patients.
No abstract. COMPETITION, INSURANCE AND QUALITY in the advanced infertility market — the supply-side companion to the AER 2018 structural paper.
Age at menopause and preceding fecundity. A.15/A.21's.
Ethics commentary arguing AGAINST mandated IVF coverage. Normative, but worth noting the frame contains advocacy on both sides of the policy.
